seoTitle: How to Delete Old TradingView Chart Layouts
metaDescription: Learn how to find and permanently remove saved chart layouts on TradingView desktop and mobile to keep your workspace organized.
intro: If you've built up too many saved chart layouts on TradingView, cleaning them up can make your workspace easier to navigate. This guide covers finding your saved layouts, opening the layout management panel, and removing the ones you no longer need.

steps.heading: Find your saved layouts
steps.body: Open the layouts menu on TradingView to see a list of every chart layout you've saved.

steps.heading: Open the layout management panel
steps.body: Select the option to manage layouts, which gives you access to rename, organize, or delete existing setups.

steps.heading: Delete unwanted layouts
steps.body: Choose the specific layout you want to remove and permanently delete it from your account.

steps.heading: Repeat for multiple layouts
steps.body: You can go through and remove several old or unused layouts in the same session to declutter your workspace.

steps.heading: Works on free and paid accounts
steps.body: This layout management process is available whether you're on a free or paid TradingView plan.

steps.heading: Keep your workspace organized
steps.body: Renaming and organizing your remaining layouts can further improve your workflow across stocks, crypto, forex, or indices.

faq.question: Can I delete a TradingView layout permanently?
faq.answer: Yes, you can permanently remove a saved layout from the layout management panel.

faq.question: Does layout deletion work the same on mobile?
faq.answer: Yes, you can manage and delete layouts from both the desktop version and the mobile app.

faq.question: Is this feature available on the free plan?
faq.answer: Yes, both free and paid TradingView users can manage and delete their saved layouts.

faq.question: Can I rename layouts instead of deleting them?
faq.answer: Yes, the layout management panel also lets you rename layouts to keep them better organized.

faq.question: Why would I delete old layouts?
faq.answer: Removing unused layouts keeps your workspace tidy, especially if you test multiple strategies or chart setups.
